fact.box: global equity index fund in a TFSA or RRSP
fact.claim: The MSCI ACWI index of large and mid-size companies in 47 countries returned 7.31% a year in US dollars from Dec 29, 2000 to Oct 30, 2026, with dividends reinvested. Over that time it also fell 58% from 2007 to 2009, and some years were negative. Index funds charge fees, and Canadians see returns in Canadian dollars, so real results will differ. MSCI says past performance does not guarantee future returns, so the 7.31% is an example rate, not a promise.

plain.what: MSCI ACWI is an index, a list of the biggest companies, bought all at once, from 47 countries around the world. From late 2000 to October 2026, it grew about 7.31% a year in US dollars, counting the money companies paid out and putting it back in. It was not a smooth ride, though: it fell 58% from 2007 to 2009, and some years went down.
plain.so_what: If you had $10,000, one year of waiting meant missing about $731 of growth at that rate. That 7.31% comes from the past, so it is only an example and not a promise.
plain.do: Write down an amount you have in mind, then work out 7.31% of it to see what one year of waiting might have cost in the past.
